question: According to Transparency International’s latest Corruption Perceptions Index, which reviews 180 countries, the EU has an average corruption rate, owing to the vast differences between the cleanest Member States, such as Denmark, which scored 90/100, and those towards the bottom of the ranking, such as Hungary, which scored just 42/100.

Despite the fact that some countries, such as Italy, are taking measures to improve transparency in the public sector, the European average is still unsatisfactory and, according to the study, efforts to tackle corruption appear to be being blocked or even scaled back in more than three quarters of European countries. In view of the above, what steps will the Commission take to cut corruption levels in Europe?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.4.2024) As the President of the Commission highlighted in her State of the Union Address1 on 14 September 2022, the fight against corruption is a key priority for the Commission. The Commission monitors and reports annually on developments, both positive and negative, regarding the fight against corruption in all Member States.

The fourth EU Rule of Law report, published on 5 July 2023, reports on the situation in each Member State and provides them with concrete recommendations to tackle systemic weaknesses2. The Commission presented on 3 May 2023 a package of measures to strengthen the EU’s capacity to fight corruption.

This includes a proposal for a Directive to modernise the existing EU anti-corruption legal framework by better preventing, investigating and prosecuting corruption offences3. Novelties also include an EU network against corruption, bringing together law enforcement, public authorities, practitioners, civil society and other stakeholders.

It was tasked to develop best practices and practical guidance and support a more systematic gathering of data and evidence that can serve as a solid basis for anticorruption actions and for monitoring the success of these actions4. Finally, the Commission will continue to use the Conditionality Regime5 in cases when breaches of the rule of law principles affect or risk affecting the EU financial interests.

Council Framework Decision 2003/568/JHA and the Convention on the fight against corruption involving officials of the European Communities or officials of Member States of the European Union and amending Directive (EU) 2017/1371 of the European Parliament and of the Council, COM(2023)234 final. 4 Joint Communication to the European Parliament.

the Council and the European Economic and Social Committee on the fight against corruption, JOIN (2023)12 final. 5 Regulation (EU, Euratom) 2020/2092 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2020 on a general regime of conditionality for the protection of the Union budget, OJ L 433I, 22.12.2020.
